lectures.title: Sample Hash Functions and Their Properties

cues.en: Now, in the previous lecture we have learned about hash terminologies.
Basically, we have learned that hash functions is the function which takes the key and converts it
to the hash value.
And based on this hash value, we are inserting the key and value pairs to the array.
Now in this lecture let's look at the sample hash functions.
Now the first one is going to be for integers.
And the second one is going to be the for string.
Now let's get started with the first one.
Now the simplest hash function is mod function which works only for integers.
Now what does this function do?
So let's say we have a key and value pairs like this.
So key is 700 and the value is 15.
And we want to insert this one by using this mod hash function to this hash table.
So in this case key is 700.
We are going to pass key as a 700.
And we know that the size of this hash table is seven.
So we are going to pass as a second parameter seven.
Then this function will return the remainder that comes from the division of this number.
So key is 700.
700 divided by seven is going to be 100 and the remainder is zero.
So this means that we can take this key and value pair and save it inside the this hash table over here
at the index of zero.
Now this is the simplest form of hash function because here as you can see we might have many collisions.
That's why it is a very simple hash table.
So here I'm just giving you an example how the logic works inside the hash table.
So let's say we take another pair.
So in this case we have 600 as a key.
So I'm just going to pass 600.
Then it's going to be table size seven.
So if we divide it the remainder is going to be five.
So this means that we can take this key and value pair insert it to the at the index of five.
So as you can see, whenever we are taking the key as an integer, we are reducing it.
For example 600 reduced to five.
Now you might be interested why we are reducing it, because our array over here has a smaller indexes.
So we need to insert them based on this index.
That's why there is no index of 600 over here.
So we have to decrease it to match the indexes over here.
So whenever you divide 600 by seven the remainder is going to be always five.
So it's not going to change.
So we are going to insert this key and value pair based on this index to this hash table.
Now this is the simplest form of hash table.
Now let's look at the second function.
So in this function the key is going to be the string.
And we need to convert it to the number.
So let's say we have a key and value pairs like this ABC as a key and value is 15.
Now if you look at this function you might see that here we find the Ascii values of characters and
sum them.
And at the end we find the index by dividing it with the table size, and we are returning the remainder
over here as well.
Now we need to take into account that in real world hash functions are complicated than this one over
here, but the basics remain the same.
Here I'm just explaining you the very simple one, to make the things more clear.
Now, in this case, if you pass ABC over here, it's going to find the Ascii values of the ABC.
Now in this table it shows the Ascii values of each character.
So in our case we have ABC.
Now ABC is located over here.
As you can see the value is 6566 and 67.
Now if I just take them and some of them based on this loop.
So as you can see, this loop loops through the characters and find their Ascii value and sum up them.
And after summing up them, it's going to be 198 and the table size is seven.
So if I divide 198 by seven, it's going to be 28 and the remainder is two.
So this means that we can take this key and value pair.
Save it in our hash table like this at the index of two.
So this is how the second hash function works now.
Hopefully you have understood the basic logic.
Now one more time I want to mention that in real life, hash functions are more complicated than this
one.
Now let's look at some properties of a good hash function.
A good hash function distributes hash values uniformly across the hash table.
This means that whenever we have a key and value pairs like this, and we set mongo as an input to this
hash function.
For example, for this one it's going to return one.
Then we have the second value pair.
For this one it's going to return three.
And then we have the third one orange.
And for this one it's going to return five.
So as you can see this hash function distributes them distributes them without any collision.
So if I just have the another key and value pair and get the number of three for this one as well.
In this case it's going to cause collusion.
So if we have more collusion in our hash tables this means that this is not a good hash table.
Now the second property is that hash table uses all input data.
Now what does it mean.
So let's say we want to pass as a key banana.
So if the hash table only uses only three characters of this string, it means that it's not using all
input data.
So it has to use all characters that we have provided over here to find out the value.
So for example in this case we have three A's.
It has to use all three A's and two N's over here.
So if it does not use all characters it means that the possibility of collisions is going to be high.
That's why it's not going to be a good hash function.
So here it has to use all characters of the string that we are passing to the hash function.
That's all for hash function.
Now in the next lecture we are going to look at the collision resolution techniques.
So see you in the next lecture.
